$comment: Dispatcher configurations. Every strategy here is a weight vector over the same scoring engine — adding a strategy is a config entry, not a class. See docs/06-parameterization-and-tuning.md.

normalization.$comment: Normalize every term to a comparable scale before weighting. Without it, waitTime (0-120s) and stopCount (0-20) yield uninterpretable weights and an unsearchable space.

profiles.$comment: The energy proxy is stopCount plus distanceTravelled, and the cheapest joule is the one an empty car never spends: parkingStrategy stay is the whole of this profile's stage 7. A longer adaptive dwell trades a little wait for fewer stops, which is the same trade in the door machine.
profiles.name: Energy aware

profiles.$comment: Weighting starvation is only half of fairness; the other half is keeping a call movable for as long as possible, so this profile takes the latest commitment point and the largest reassignment budget of any profile here, and turns on the sole-eligible-car override so a floor served by one shaft cannot be skipped indefinitely on load.
profiles.name: Fairness first

profiles.$comment: The profile the capacity mechanisms are named for, so it declares all three: split-demand for parallel service at a heavy landing, until-commitment reassignment so a car crossing its bypass threshold hands its uncommitted calls on, and the sole-eligible-car override so the guard against a starved floor is on while it does.
profiles.name: Capacity aware

profiles.$comment: Contract-net bidding: every car prices the contract from its own estimateCost() and the group allocates from the bids. ONE profile, deliberately, because the aggregation is auction.rounds and config/schema.ts has no auction section yet — so a second profile could not carry a different aggregation, it would resolve to rounds = 1 and be this profile under another name. Both arms of the comparison are therefore built from THIS profile: createAuctionPolicy(profile) is rounds = 1, the sealed-bid single round, which IS the centralized argmin over the same weight vector and is the control arm; createAuctionPolicy(profile, { auction: { rounds: 3, reserveMarginalDelayS: 25 } }) is the contract net, in which a provisional winner may take its bid back on its own reserve price or because winning would push it over its own hall-call bypass threshold while another bidder stays under. Same weights, same seven stages, same everything except who aggregates — which is what makes a paired-t interval between them an interval on the aggregation. Comparing two different profiles instead would measure whatever stage settings they differed in and exactly zero aggregation, and a benchmark of sealed-bid against the weighted-cost engine must return exactly zero. reassignmentPolicy is until-commitment on both arms: a car that may hand a contract back must also be allowed to lose one, and a stage-5 setting that differed between the arms would be the confound.
profiles.name: Contract-net auction

profiles.$comment: Operational zoning — the third kind, a dispatcher strategy and not building fabric. The bank is partitioned into one contiguous band per in-service car; zoneAffinity prices a car's deviation from its band. The partition is computed per decision by the dispatcher, never stored on a car: a car that owned its zone could not be re-zoned when a neighbour goes out of service. Split-demand at ten is the up-peak half — a lobby landing above one carload is two cars, not one car twice. parkingStrategy is stay, NOT zone-center, and that is a measured decision rather than a default: Simulation.#park builds its RepositionContext from entranceFloorIds alone, so zone-center gets no partition, every car computes the same shaft median, and on midtown-office at DISPATCH_DEFAULTS all four cars are sent to floor 10 — the outcome zoning.ts itself calls worse than not parking. Through prepositionPlan, which supplies the partition, the same bank gets one target per band, 2/7/12/17, and three cars move (the fourth is inside its own deadband). When #park passes repositionContextFor(car, resolvePrepositionContext(...)), set parkingStrategy back to zone-center with repositionThresholdS 2 and repositionEnergyWeight 0.1; policies.test.ts asserts today that no shipped profile sends two cars of a bank to one floor under the context the runner actually supplies.
profiles.name: Operational zoning, up-peak

patternSwitching.$comment: Per-pattern weight sets. The optimum for up-peak is not the optimum for down-peak. Hysteresis prevents detector oscillation.
